target.title: feat(agent): preserve interrupted-turn context and anchor session recall on search hits
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two long-session truthfulness/recall gaps, found by a structured survey of leading agent-runtime internals (designs ported, no code copied):

1. **Aborted turns lie by omission.** After `/stop` or steering aborts a tool-running turn, the transcript records only an empty aborted assistant message. The next provider request carries no signal that tools may have partially executed, so the model assumes clean completion and repeats or skips side-effecting work. Codex CLI ships a `<turn_aborted>` context fragment for exactly this (`codex-rs/core/src/context/turn_aborted.rs`).
2. **Search hits are dead ends.** `sessions_search` returns a stable `messageId`, but `sessions_history` can only tail/offset-page, so a hit buried in an older (or pre-reset archived) session cannot be reopened in one call. The fix is anchoring a bounded window around the hit id.

Closes #105828. Closes #105829.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both fixes serve one story: long-running multi-turn work should stay truthful when interrupted and recoverable when searched.

- **Interrupted-turn truth** (`packages/agent-core`): every abort path (loop abort, loop failure, agent failure, harness failure) appends a hidden `openclaw:turn-aborted` custom message. It is normalized to a user-role text message immediately before provider conversion, so the model sees the guidance on the next turn while channel-visible history stays clean. Append-only, preserving prompt-cache prefixes.
- **Anchored session recall** (`sessions_history` + `chat.history`): the tool accepts a search hit's `sessionId` + `messageId`, validates session ownership, and the gateway reads one anchor-centered page from a single stable transcript snapshot (active or reset-archive), byte-capped by growing around the anchor. Anchored responses deliberately expose no offset cursor/pagination metadata: numeric offsets cannot encode which archived transcript the anchor resolved to, so handing one out would corrupt subsequent paging. This composes with #105688's offset paging — anchored reads are a separate `pagination`-less arm of the same `readChatHistoryPage` gate, and CLI-import-bound sessions fall through to the full-snapshot merge where the handler-level cap still centers on the anchor.

## User Impact

- After stopping or steering mid-run, the agent checks state instead of assuming aborted commands completed (or silently duplicating them).
- Cross-session recall becomes one-step: search, then reopen the surrounding conversation directly, including sessions archived by `/new`.

## Evidence

- Real-runtime gateway proof on the final head `883c7c600ce` (Blacksmith Testbox, Linux Node 24: built gateway process, real WS protocol client, real session store + SQLite FTS; scripted OpenAI-compatible provider so request payloads are ground truth): (a) abort a held-open turn via `chat.abort`, follow-up provider request contains the interruption/partial-execution guidance; (b) bury an anchor behind seven later turns, confirm the tail omits it, find it via live SQLite FTS, reopen a five-message neighborhood by `sessionId` + `messageId` with no offset cursor exposed.
- New behavior tests: agent-loop abort marker paths, anchored/`sessionId` validation and windowing in `sessions-history-tool` + gateway protocol, anchored `chat.history` (bounded page, reset-archive anchor, offset+messageId rejection, foreign `sessionId` rejection).
- Affected sweep (agent-core, gateway-protocol, sessions tools, transcript readers, gateway chat, config/sessions) green after rebase onto `main` (post-#105688 offset-paging integration; anchored reads are a separate pagination-less arm of the same read gate); `tsgo` lanes green; `check:changed` lanes green incl. Plugin SDK API baseline regen; protocol schema + Swift models and prompt snapshots regenerated; SDK surface budgets unchanged; fresh autoreview clean. Full verdict JSON in the proof comment below.
